name: Stony Point
intro: Stony Point is the smallest possible village  -  a jetty, a ferry terminal, a railway terminus, a fishermen's hut or two  -  and one of the most useful addresses on the Peninsula. The ferry from the jetty runs across Western Port to French Island and on to Cowes on Phillip Island, which makes Stony Point one of the few places on mainland Victoria you can step off a train and onto a boat. There is no town to wander  -  the village is barely a village  -  but the working pier is a real fishing community and the views across to French Island catch the afternoon light beautifully. Park here, walk the jetty, take the ferry, or just sit on the pier with fish and chips brought down from Hastings. Stony Point is a transit point that rewards being treated as a destination for a few hours.
factualLede: Stony Point is the southern terminus of the Stony Point railway line on the Mornington Peninsula's Western Port coast, 85 km from Melbourne, with a working fishing jetty and a passenger ferry to French Island and Phillip Island.

heroImage.alt: The Stony Point jetty and ferry across Western Port to French Island in the distance

tldr: Stony Point is a jetty, a ferry terminal and a train terminus — the rare Australian point where you step off a train and onto a boat.
Best for: French Island day trippers; Phillip Island connectors; carless travellers who want to leave the car at Frankston.
Signature experience: train to Stony Point, ferry to French Island for a cycle, ferry back, fish and chips on the jetty.
Half a day for the ferry loop; a full day including French Island.
There is nothing to eat at the terminal — bring it from Hastings.
notFor: anyone expecting a village to wander
stayDuration: half a day for the ferry loop
signature: The only point in Victoria where you step off a train and onto a ferry across Western Port.
skip: Trying to find a café — Stony Point is a jetty, not a village.
bestDay: Morning train from Frankston, ferry across to French Island, hire a bike at Tankerton, late ferry back, fish and chips on the jetty waiting for the train home.
insiderNote: Check the ferry timetable carefully — sailings are limited and tide-dependent, and missing the last boat back is a long taxi from Cowes.
